## Introduction

In this post, I would like to figure out the difference of penguin's body mass 
across different species.I will use python as the analysis tool to compare body
mass across Adelie, Chinstrap, and Gentoo penguins.

Data source: [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/),
collected and made available by Dr. Kristen Gorman and
Palmer Station Antarctica LTER. The data are available under
the [CC0 license](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/).
I access the data through the Python `palmerpenguins` package.

Original study: Gorman, K. B., Williams, T. D., and Fraser, W. R.
(2014). Ecological sexual dimorphism and environmental variability
within a community of Antarctic penguins (genus Pygoscelis).
[PLOS ONE, 9(3), e90081](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0090081).

## Load and inspect the data

First, I load the dataset and inspect its dimensions and first five rows.

```{python}
#| label: load-data
#| warning: false

import sys
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

print("Python executable:", sys.executable)

penguins = load_penguins()
print("Rows and columns:", penguins.shape)
penguins.head()
```

## Clean the data

For this comparison, I need species and body mass. I remove rows
with missing values in either column, while keeping rows that
have missing values in unrelated columns.

```{python}
#| label: clean-data

mass_data = penguins.dropna(subset=["species", "body_mass_g"]).copy()

print("Original rows:", len(penguins))
print("Rows kept:", len(mass_data))
print("Rows removed:", len(penguins) - len(mass_data))
```

## Summarize body mass by species

I calculate the sample size, mean, and median body mass for each
species. Body mass is measured in grams.

```{python}
#| label: summarize-mass

mass_summary = (
    mass_data.groupby("species")
    .agg(
        sample_size=("body_mass_g", "count"),
        mean_mass_g=("body_mass_g", "mean"),
        median_mass_g=("body_mass_g", "median")
    )
    .round(1)
)

mass_summary
```

## Visualize average body mass

The chart compares mean body mass across species. The vertical
axis starts at zero so that bar heights represent the differences
proportionally.

```{python}
#| label: fig-mean-mass
#| fig-cap: "Mean body mass by penguin species, excluding records with missing species or body mass."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))

ax.bar(
    mass_summary.index,
    mass_summary["mean_mass_g"],
    color=["#4477AA", "#EE6677", "#228833"]
)

ax.set_xlabel("Species")
ax.set_ylabel("Mean body mass (g)")
ax.set_title("Average body mass by penguin species")
ax.set_ylim(bottom=0)

fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Conclusion

Among the 342 penguins with non-missing species and body mass,
Gentoo penguins have the highest mean body mass (5,076.0 g).
Adelie and Chinstrap penguins have similar mean body masses
of 3,700.7 g and 3,733.1 g, respectively.

These results describe the penguins in this dataset. The chart
compares group averages but does not show variation within each
species. This analysis also does not account for sex or other
factors that may be associated with body mass.
